title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from Th. 1.1 and 1.6 on the previous page). X and Y are smooth projective connected varieties over an algebraically closed field k, of dimensions n and m. Z is a cycle of codimension n on X×Y, so dim Z = m and its fibres Z_y over points y ∈ Y are 0-cycles on X.
- Th. 1.1 attaches to Z a homomorphism of Albanese varieties u_Z : A_Y → A_X, essentially y ↦ alb_X(Z_y − Z_{y0}).
- Th. 1.6 says that the action of the ℓ-adic class γ^n(Z) ∈ H^{2n}(X×Y)(n) on H^1 is compatible with u_Z. The correspondence is a(γ^n(Z)) : H^1(X,Z_ℓ) → H^1(Y,Z_ℓ): pull back, cup with the class, push forward along X. Compatibility means a(γ^n(Z))∘φ_X^* = φ_Y^*∘u_Z^{(1)}, where φ^* are the maps induced by the Albanese morphisms.

Corollary 1.7 (this page) specialises to X, Y abelian varieties, so that A_X = X, A_Y = Y and φ_X^*, φ_Y^* are isomorphisms. Then a Z_ℓ-linear map φ : H^1(X) → H^1(Y) is induced by an algebraic cycle of codimension n on X×Y if and only if φ = u^{(1)} = u^* for a homomorphism of abelian varieties u : Y → X.
- Necessity: this is Th. 1.6 with u = u_Z.
- Sufficiency: take Z = the transpose of the graph Γ_u ⊂ Y×X. It has dimension m, i.e. codimension n in X×Y.
Moreover, for fixed Z, u = u_Z is uniquely determined and independent of ℓ. This holds because u_Z is defined algebraically via the Albanese map, and Hom(Y,X) → Hom(H^1(X,Z_ℓ), H^1(Y,Z_ℓ)) is injective (Weil). So the cycle-theoretic image of codimension-n correspondences acting on H^1 is exactly Hom(Y,X), ℓ-independently.

Remark 1.8 sketches a relative version of 1.1 over an arbitrary base S:
- X and Y are smooth projective over S with geometrically connected fibres.
- Z is an 'n-cocycle' in CK^n(X×_S Y). This is a cycle group defined via the graded ring associated to a filtration on K-theory, used because naive cycles and intersections are not available over a general base.
- One obtains A_Y → A_X when the relative Albanese schemes exist.
- Continued on the next page: more generally, if A_Y exists and one is given a morphism from X to a torsor ('schéma parabélien') under an abelian scheme A, one gets A_Y → A. This comes through an element of CH^1(A_Y × A^*), a divisorial correspondence, i.e. a family of line bundles. On geometric fibres it agrees with the construction of 1.1.

Purpose: this is a preparatory section for §2, which proves the algebraicity of certain homomorphisms between abelian varieties (Picard/Albanese) using ℓ-adic cohomology. It belongs to Grothendieck's programme on the standard conjectures, Hodge, Tate and Lefschetz, where H^1 is the known case.
errors: No genuine error. The equivalence and uniqueness are classical (Weil). Uniqueness of u given φ needs injectivity of Hom(Y,X) → Hom(T_ℓ). This is standard but not stated as an input on this page.

On the previous page, the hedge 'iso mod torsion si ...' for φ_X^* : H^1(A_X,Z_ℓ) → H^1(X,Z_ℓ) is unnecessary with Z_ℓ coefficients: H^1(X,Z_ℓ) is torsion-free and the map is an isomorphism. For abelian X it is trivially an isomorphism, which is what 1.7 uses.
Remark 1.8 is only a sketch. The intersection/K-theoretic definition of CK^n over a general base, and the existence of relative Albanese schemes, are assumed without discussion.

ideas.what: For abelian varieties, the action on H^1 of algebraic codimension-n correspondences on X×Y is exactly given by homomorphisms Y→X; u is determined by Z and independent of ℓ
ideas.modern_name: H^1 case of the Tate/Hodge-type description of correspondences; Weil's theory of correspondences between abelian varieties; injectivity Hom(Y,X)⊗Z_ℓ → Hom(T_ℓY,T_ℓX)
ideas.usually_credited_to: A. Weil (Variétés abéliennes et courbes algébriques, 1948); Lang, Abelian Varieties
ideas.where_published: Related material in Grothendieck's 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969), where H^1 is the known case; not this precise statement

ideas.what: Correspondence Z of codim n on X×Y inducing u_Z : A_Y → A_X compatibly with the ℓ-adic correspondence on H^1
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of the Albanese/Picard variety under correspondences; compatibility of cycle class with Albanese

ideas.what: Relative version over an arbitrary base S, using K-theoretic cycle groups CK^n(X×_S Y) (graded ring associated to K) to define correspondences inducing maps of relative Albanese schemes or into torsors under abelian schemes, via CH^1(A_Y × A^*)
ideas.modern_name: Relative correspondences / relative Albanese functoriality; K-theoretic Chow groups (gr of the γ- or topological filtration, SGA 6)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Berthelot–Illusie (SGA 6) for the filtrations on K; relative Albanese: Grothendieck (FGA), later Deligne and others
ideas.where_published: SGA 6 for gr K; the specific relative-correspondence statement: unsure

missed.claim: A sketched relative theory of correspondences over an arbitrary base. Cycles are taken in the graded ring associated to K-theory of X×_S Y, and induce morphisms of relative Albanese schemes, or into torsors ('schémas parabéliens') under abelian schemes, via divisorial correspondences. It is left as a remark without proof.
missed.quote: Généralisation de 1.1. aux schémas projectifs lisses, à fibres géom. connexes, sur une base quelconque S, en partant d'un n-cocycle (au sens du gradué associé au K) Z ∈ CK^n(X×_S Y)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor point: relative Albanese functoriality and relative correspondences are now handled by other means (bivariant intersection theory, relative motives). It shows an early intention to use K-theoretic cycles over general bases for this purpose, but such a use is probably not new to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: Corollary 1.7 is a classical consequence of Weil's theory. Remark 1.8 is a brief sketch of a relative generalisation using K-theoretic cycles, which is natural for Grothendieck around SGA 6 and is now standard in spirit.
transcription_corrections: 'indépendant du choix [?] premier ℓ choisi' should read roughly 'indépendant du nombre premier ℓ choisi pour les coefficients dans la cohomologie' (abbreviated 'nb premier').
'(au sens de la généralisation associée au K)' should read '(au sens du gradué associé au K)', i.e. the graded ring associated to a filtration on K-theory.
'(plus que, si A_Y existe' is likely '(plus gén., si A_Y existe', i.e. 'plus généralement'.
'sur un base quelconque S [-...-]' should read 'sur une base quelconque S'; a crossed-out symbol follows S.
'de [-de-] codim n' reads 'de [crossed-out] codim n sur X×Y'.
In 'Généralisation de 1.1.', the 'de 1.1.' is an insertion above the line.
